title: Mem0
by: Mem0 (mem0ai), a Y Combinator company. Read from its README, its prompts (mem0/configs/prompts.py), the add/update/delete/history code in mem0/memory/main.py, and its v2-to-v3 migration guide. The paper 'Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory' (arXiv 2504.19413) was not read: arxiv.org was blocked; only a search summary of its abstract was seen.
summary: A memory layer that extracts facts from conversations. Its classic design let a model choose one of four operations for each new fact against similar old ones: ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NONE (the paper calls it NOOP). In April 2026 the open-source version moved to ADD-only extraction: nothing is overwritten, new memories link to related old ones, and retrieval ranks the right dated memory. Every change is written to a history table.
ideas: The classic update step: a model compares each new fact with similar stored ones and returns an event per memory: ADD, UPDATE (with old_memory), DELETE or NONE.
v3 is ADD-only: one model call, no UPDATE or DELETE; a new memory lists linked_memory_ids of the older ones it continues or changes.
The project reports large benchmark gains from going ADD-only (LoCoMo 71.4 to 92.5, LongMemEval 67.8 to 94.4 on its managed platform), so letting a model overwrite memory cost accuracy.
Each memory has a history of events (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE) with old and new value, read with history(memory_id).
Memories are scoped by user_id, agent_id and run_id; facts the agent itself confirms are stored with the same weight as the user's.
Retrieval fuses semantic, keyword (BM25) and entity matches, and handles time by picking the right dated instance.

took.idea: Append only: a new doc never edits an old one; it links to what it changes
A closed set of operation names returned for every write
A per-doc history of events with old and new value
